subject: Mixing Force Constants In DISANG Files

messages.author: Sharif Nada
messages.body:
Hello all,
I am working on a project where I am writing my own dihedral restraints
rather than using makeANG_RST or makeCHIR_RST. I have copied the
general syntax of the output of these programs where the first entry
has an additional line specifying the force constants:
&rst iat = 3, 4, 5, 22,
r1 = -108.3812, r2 = -38.3812, r3 = -38.3812, r4 = 31.6188,
rk2 = 1.0, rk3 = 1.0, /
And subsequent entries omit the force constant:
&rst iat = 5, 6, 7, 9,
r1 = -108.8825, r2 = -38.8825, r3 = -38.8825, r4 = 31.1175,
/
My question is how the code would interpret an input such as:
&rst iat = 3, 4, 5, 22,
r1 = -108.3812, r2 = -38.3812, r3 = -38.3812, r4 = 31.6188,
rk2 = 1.0, rk3 = 1.0,
&rst iat = 5, 6, 7, 9,
r1 = -108.8825, r2 = -38.8825, r3 = -38.8825, r4 = 31.1175,
rk2 = 1.5, rk3 = 1.5,
/
Would Amber read only the first or last value specified for rk2 and
rk3, or is it possible to assign different values of rk2 and rk3 for
each restraint in this way?
Thanks,
Sharif

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
Yes that's fine to specify the force constants for each, and they can
differ. If not specified, the prior ones are used. You're doing the right
thing.

messages.author: Sharif Nada
messages.body:
Hello all,
I have been trying to adjust the "softness" of the softcore vdw
potentials in both Amber 18 and 20 by varying the value of scalpha, but
I do not seem to be seeing any changes in the calculated energies in
the log file as I change the values of the parameter. I also checked
the outputted forces and saw they were indeed exactly the same with two
different values of scalpha. I was wondering if any developers or
experienced users of the softcore code would know what could be causing
this. I am happy to provide the files I used in my tests if they would
be of any help.
Best regards,
Sharif
